title: Nominalisation
grammar_goal: Elevates Grammatical Range and Vocabulary to Band 7+ by transforming verbs/adjectives into nouns, a hallmark of formal academic writing.

core_rule.usage: Nominalisation allows you to discuss concepts and abstract ideas rather than specific people doing specific actions. It shifts the focus from the 'doer' to the 'action/concept' itself, which is essential for an objective academic tone.

when_to_use: Task 2: Throughout the essay to maintain an objective tone (e.g., 'The consumption of fast food...' instead of 'People consume fast food...').
Task 1: Describing trends where the noun form is needed for variety (e.g., 'There was a significant fluctuation in...' instead of 'The prices fluctuated significantly.').
when_not_to_use: Avoid overusing it in Speaking Part 1 or 2, as it can sound excessively formal and robotic (e.g., 'My enjoyment of the movie was high' instead of 'I really enjoyed the movie').
Do not nominalise every single verb in a sentence, as it leads to 'noun disease', making the sentence heavy and difficult to read.

ielts_examples.writing: The implementation of stricter environmental laws has led to a noticeable reduction in urban air pollution.
ielts_examples.speaking: I think the accessibility of education in rural areas is a major issue right now.

repair_section.wrong: Because they destroyed the forest, many animals lost their homes.
repair_section.correct: The destruction of the forest caused many animals to lose their habitats.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: The extensive deforestation resulted in a catastrophic loss of animal habitats.

repair_section.wrong: People rely on technology too much, which is dangerous.
repair_section.correct: The over-reliance on technology is dangerous.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: Society's excessive dependence on technological devices poses significant risks.

vietnamese_learner_mistakes: Sticking to S-V-O structures (Subject-Verb-Object) because Vietnamese grammar rarely uses suffixes to change word classes.
Using the wrong preposition after the nominalised noun (e.g., 'The development for the city' instead of 'The development of the city').
Inventing incorrect noun forms (e.g., 'The destroyment' instead of 'The destruction').

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: When the economy grows, it helps the country.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: The growth of the economy helps the country.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: The government needs to invest in schools to improve education.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: Government investment in schools is necessary for the improvement of education.

image_prompt_fallback: A visual metaphor showing a flowing liquid (representing a verb/action) being frozen into a solid block (representing a noun/concept).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses nominalisation to create a formal academic tone?

options.A: If we produce more food locally, the environment will be better.
options.B: Producing more food locally makes the environment better.
options.C: An increase in local food production leads to environmental improvement.
options.D: When food is produced locally more, the environment improves.

quiz.explanation: Option C transforms the verbs 'produce' and 'improve' into the nouns 'production' and 'improvement', resulting in a highly objective and formal academic sentence.
